The most common win left on "Patriotic Payout" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $500, and 119 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Tomorrow's count on "Patriotic Payout" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2776.headline: What the prize table shows

2779.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Gnome for the Holidays", nearly all are still unsold. The game is near the start of its run, with 56 of 57 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The numbers for "Gnome for the Holidays" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2779.headline: Early stage or late

2780.body:
"Holiday Countdown" just went on sale in Texas. The game has ten full prize levels with five top prizes of $100,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

Every line of Holiday Countdown's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2780.headline: A new game is here

2781.body:
"The Perfect Gift" just reached Texas stores with five top prizes of $250,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

The numbers for "The Perfect Gift" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2781.headline: First day on sale

2782.body:
"$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" has joined the Texas lineup at $20 with four top prizes of $1 million. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

If "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2782.headline: A brand-new game to watch
